traceability.requirement: Later language features identify whether they are source syntax, core semantics, compiler behavior, runtime behavior, package policy, artifact schema, or governance policy.
traceability.evidence_expectation: A minimal source program can be traced from source forms through syntax, typed core, selected runtime, and provenance records.

traceability.requirement: Every profile states allowed behavior, rejected behavior, delegated behavior, required checks, and emitted evidence before backend lowering.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Accepted and rejected profile fixtures prove legality before target lowering.

traceability.requirement: Dangerous operations are classified as proven safe, runtime checked, rejected, or unsafe island with audit metadata.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Safety fixtures include accepted safe code, rejected unsafe code, runtime-checked cases, and unsafe audit records.

traceability.requirement: Schemas, AI agents, workflows, proofs, diagnostics, build outputs, and package metadata are first-class artifacts with provenance.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Every emitted artifact records source identity, compiler identity, profile, target, effects, capabilities, safety status, and provenance.

traceability.requirement: The bootstrap path reduces trusted code over time through reproducibility and equivalence evidence.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Stage records include source hashes, artifact hashes, compiler identities, and permitted difference reports.

traceability.requirement: The reader, macro expansion, semantic checks, MIR, domain IRs, optimization, lowering, emission, and provenance steps expose equivalent pass facts even when fused.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Pipeline fixtures show required facts before each consuming pass and reject out-of-order consumption.

traceability.requirement: Every domain IR preserves a semantic anchor to typed core or MIR and emits auditable artifacts.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Domain IR examples include typed-core or MIR anchors and rejected unanchored artifacts.

traceability.requirement: Runtime selection is a consequence of profile and target, not an implicit compiler default.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Runtime manifests show required services and no-runtime artifacts prove absence of undeclared services.

traceability.requirement: Each milestone compiles something real, rejects something real, emits artifacts, and records diagnostics before support is claimed.
traceability.evidence_expectation: A milestone bundle cannot pass unless positive fixtures, negative fixtures, diagnostics, artifacts, and open risks are present.

traceability.requirement: Implementation follows the critical chain from D0 through BOOT1 unless later work consumes documented interfaces without claiming release status.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Roadmap updates cite the governing upstream contracts and do not mark downstream support without upstream evidence.

traceability.requirement: Normative text and artifacts keep profile distinct from target, effect from capability, runtime from backend, and artifact from file.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Terminology fixtures accept D3-aligned records and reject concept conflation in manifests and diagnostics.

traceability.requirement: Compiler, runtime, package, tooling, and governance artifacts use stable D3 concept names for profile, target, effect, capability, safety mode, and provenance.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Artifact schemas and diagnostics share the D3 vocabulary without backend-specific translation.

traceability.requirement: Every coverage claim names domain, profiles, accepted subset, effects, capabilities, artifacts, and a credible replacement slice.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Coverage reports distinguish implemented, designed, delegated, and out-of-scope slices.

traceability.requirement: Interop boundaries are typed, effect-annotated, capability-gated, profile-legal, audited if unsafe, represented in artifacts, and fixture-covered.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Interop fixtures include accepted boundaries and rejected untracked external behavior.

traceability.requirement: Replacement claims specify incumbent family, Gravity profiles, targets, supported slice, unsupported slice, interop boundaries, artifacts, tests, and performance expectations.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Replacement records cannot pass without accepted and rejected fixtures for the claimed slice.

traceability.requirement: Replacement and migration cannot bypass type, effect, profile, capability, memory, safety, package, or artifact checks.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Migrated or generated code must pass the same safety/profile checks as handwritten code.

traceability.requirement: Performance claims name profile, target, runtime, backend, safety mode, layout, input domain, erased checks, proof obligations, and benchmark method.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Benchmark evidence records source hash, compiler identity, target fingerprint, optimization manifest, sample count, and baseline.

traceability.requirement: Optimizations preserve, regenerate, retain, or reject safety facts and never erase checks without surviving proof.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Optimization fixtures cover preserved proof, regenerated proof, retained runtime check, and rejected transformation.

traceability.requirement: Extensions declare kind, owner, input contract, output contract, profiles, effects, capabilities, safety mode, artifact schema, fixtures, diagnostics, version, and compatibility policy.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Extension fixtures accept declared behavior and reject missing capabilities, unsupported profiles, and undeclared build effects.

traceability.requirement: Compiler passes declare preserved facts, invalidated facts, regenerated facts, diagnostics, proof obligations, and artifacts.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Pass fixtures prove preserved and invalidated facts before downstream consumers use the output.

traceability.requirement: Every dangerous operation is classified into exactly one safety outcome: proven safe, runtime checked, rejected, or unsafe island.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Safety analysis reports include source or generated-origin spans and one legal outcome per dangerous operation.

traceability.requirement: Unsafe islands declare reason, source span, profiles, effects, capabilities, preconditions, postconditions, invariants, safe wrapper, evidence, owner, review state, and re-review policy.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Unsafe internals are eligible for safe APIs only when wrapper tests or proofs cover every precondition.

traceability.requirement: Package, build, runtime, AI, and tool systems enforce the same effect and capability authority rules as source code.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Capability fixtures reject undeclared filesystem, network, shell, database, secret, model, tool, FFI, and raw-memory authority.

traceability.requirement: Every proof or certificate names its claim, domain, assumptions, checker, inputs, and result.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Certificate fixtures include accepted checkable certificates and rejected uncheckable certificates.

traceability.requirement: Mathematical equivalence is not inferred from syntax similarity or EML tree identity alone.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Math fixtures reject EML tree identity as equality without symbolic, interval, SMT, rewrite, or approximation proof.

traceability.requirement: Replay, package, and bootstrap evidence are reproducible from recorded inputs and sufficient to audit nondeterminism and stage equivalence.
traceability.evidence_expectation: Replay fixtures do not redo nondeterministic operations, and bootstrap fixtures compare stage outputs with recorded compiler identities.
